#GoogleGemini and I had a convo about why it sucks at spatial data (and therefore has difficulty following spatial instructions). It turns out, there isn't enough open 3D spatial data models available to scrape. At the time Google sold #SketchUp, they hadn't anticipated the true value of the hundreds of thousands, even millions, of 3D models they would have had access to. Ironic, ain't it?

Could they buy up Trimble? Yes. $12B is a drop in the bucket for Google.

Would it trigger antitrust concerns? Yes. But, they could move 3D Warehouse into a public repository and allow anyone to scrape it for the same 3D spatial data to train their models.

This one move would help make AI make a massive leap forward as a visualization tool.

Is that a bad thing? I don't think so. Yes, there's a large market of workers whose job is to build models, paint textures, rig them, etc. But it will shift them to being their own creators. There'll be an explosion of small companies producing top content.
